A1.justification: Both PDFs describe d2Cache and retain matching methods, experiments, and figures. All 17 pages of v1 and 21 pages of v2, including their appendices, are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, decoding and caching ablations, and analyses of attention and KV-state dynamics on LLaDA and Dream.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds benchmark evaluations, parallel-decoding comparisons, rollout-depth ablations, and memory measurements.

M1.justification: The default two-stage algorithm and Equations (3)-(9) remain unchanged; the revised certainty-prior terminology does not alter the selection formula. Appendix D.3 adds a lightweight Rollout-5 variant that computes attention rollout using the first five Dream layers instead of all 28, a limited procedural variant rather than a replacement for the default method.

E1.justification: v2 adds GPQA and MMLU-Pro evaluations for both Base and Instruct model variants, expanding coverage from mathematical reasoning and code generation to scientific question answering and broader knowledge tasks. The original four benchmarks remain. Longer generation lengths are additional settings within retained tasks.

E2.justification: Vanilla, dLLM-Cache, and Fast-dLLM remain the principal baselines. v2 adds an uncached Parallel comparator in Table 6 and includes Semi-AR (Vanilla) in the decoding comparison in Table 2, where v1 compared only NAR configurations.

E3.justification: v2 introduces comparisons using semi-AR parallel decoding with a 0.9 threshold, Dream-Inst evaluations at generation length 1024, peak-memory measurements, and sensitivity sweeps across lengths 256, 512, and 1024. The baseline decoding settings moved into Section 5.1 were already documented in v1 Appendix B and do not establish a changed protocol for the retained experiments.

E4.justification: v2 adds a five-layer versus full-rollout ablation, parallel-decoding compatibility comparisons, and analyses of longer-generation efficiency and memory. The existing hyperparameter analysis in v1 Appendix C.4 is expanded across three generation lengths and moved to Section 5.3. The original attention, KV-trajectory, and update-phase analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, statistical significance tests, or uncertainty bars for the empirical results. The Gaussian standard deviation is a method hyperparameter, not an uncertainty estimate.

E6.justification: Beyond substantial new result entries, v2 revises retained results: Table 1 changes LLaDA-Inst MBPP scores from 14.4 to 38.0 for Vanilla and 12.4 to 39.4 for d2Cache, and d2Cache GSM8K throughput from 8.56 to 11.39. Fast-dLLM's Dream-Base MBPP score changes from 31.2 in v1 Table 4 to 52.6 in v2 Table 5. These are reported-value revisions; their cause is not explained. New parallel-decoding speedups, including 48.3x, use a different protocol and are not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Appendix D.1 adds an analytical storage calculation: 2LNd floating-point values for the KV cache plus an L-by-L attention-rollout matrix. The core mathematical definitions and Equations (1)-(9) remain unchanged, and no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: training-free acceleration through two-stage adaptive caching, more reliable certainty-guided decoding, and improved generation quality. Additional experiments broaden the supporting evidence without redefining these core contributions.

C2.justification: New Appendix D discusses memory costs, why quasi-left-to-right decoding retains diffusion-model flexibility, and limitations involving larger models, rollout approximations, and Gaussian contextual weighting. v2 also removes v1's interpretation that poor Fast-dLLM Base-model results demonstrate restricted applicability. Its new long-generation interpretation claims no performance loss, although Table 7 shows lower GSM8K and Math-500 scores than Vanilla.

D1.justification: v2 documents refresh intervals for the added benchmarks in Table 3, the parallel-decoding threshold, rollout-depth configurations, and LLM assistance with writing and coding. The hardware, evaluation framework, default sigma/k/p values, and code-access URL remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for GPQA and MMLU-Pro, two Li et al. diffusion-model works, and Zhu et al. on attentive feature regularization. It drops the specific argument that Fast-dLLM's Base-model performance restricts its applicability, while retaining the principal positioning of token-level adaptive caching against segment-level approaches.

P1.justification: Most main-text wording and the section sequence remain intact. v2 refines certainty-prior terminology, removes the Key Observations and Takeaways box, moves and condenses the hyperparameter discussion, and reorganizes the appendices around added disclosure and discussion sections. It also adds the conference-publication header.

P2.justification: v2 expands the benchmark and configuration tables, adds decoding rows to Table 2, and introduces separate rollout-depth, parallel-decoding, and long-generation/memory tables. The two-panel hyperparameter Figure 9 in v1 becomes a four-panel main-text Figure 6. Existing attention and trajectory figures are retained with renumbering and relocation.

improvement.justification: The added common-protocol parallel-decoding comparisons and rollout-depth and memory analyses address important gaps in v1's evidence about practical acceleration and its costs. Broader task coverage and explicit limitations substantially strengthen the evaluation. Reporting problems temper this improvement: substantial score revisions are unexplained, LLaDA-Inst Vanilla MBPP is 38.0 in Table 1 but 14.4 in Table 6, and the long-generation discussion overlooks math-score losses. These issues limit specific conclusions but do not negate the substantial gains from the added controls and analyses.
